newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovakia must meet criteria for NATO, EU, Kinkel says.
newsitem.headline: Slovakia must meet criteria for NATO, EU, Kinkel says.

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said on Thursday Bonn was sympathetic to Slovakia's efforts to join NATO and the EU but said it would have to fulfil all criteria for membership first.

"We feel a responsibility for the region of central an eastern Europe," Kinkel told a news conference after his first meeting with Slovak Foreign Minister Pavol Hamzik, during which he signed a cultural agreement between Bonn and Bratislava.
"But the conditions for membership are the fulfilment of all criteria, both economic and those concerning the development of democracy," Kinkel said.
Hamzik reiterated Slovakia's desire to be among the first countries invited by NATO to join the alliance at its summit in Madrid in July.
But the country's chances appear to have waned in recent months after repeated U.S. and European Union criticism, including that of Germany, over the pace of its democratic reforms.
"With regard to the negative attitude of the U.S., it makes it very unlikely that Slovakia will be in the first wave of NATO applicants," Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar said earlier this week.
He was reacting to a U.S. State Department statement last week which expressed disappointment with Slovakia's failure to carry out the type of economic and political reform expected of it.
Kinkel said NATO's Madrid summit would also include policy decisions on the reshaping of NATO from a purely defensive alliance to structures of peace keeping and peace making.
"We must also develop a strategy for helping those countries which will not be invited to join the alliance in the first round," he said.
He added that no final decision had been made on which countries would be invited to join in the first round.
Kinkel arrived in Slovakia from a two-day visit to Romania where he gave a similar message to Bucharest, which is striving to overcome long odds and win quick entry to NATO.

"As German foreign minister I cannot and will not make promises, but I am impressed by the will to join Euro-Atlantic structures as soon as possible," Kinkel told a news conference after two days of talks with Romania's new centrist leaders.
